answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, released only after three unrelated confirmations, no identity may audit its own recruit. A beacon of per-task receipts records who did what, and the terrace of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Reaching the reef of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
